On your break / On-site operations

Who looks after the meal machine?

For a site manager, catering often starts with a practical question. Who has the key, who notices an empty shelf, and who can the night shift call? Clear responsibilities make the first weeks easier.

Walk through the building together

The site partner knows how people move through the building. Together we check the proposed floor space, power connection, delivery access and whether every shift can reach the machine. A simple sketch showing the route from the entrance to the proposed position can be more informative than a plan of the entire facility.

Follow a meal from shelf to serving

Meals stay packaged and chilled inside the machine. After choosing a dish and paying without cash, the customer can have it heated inside the unit. Someone saving lunch for later can collect it chilled and follow the storage and heating instructions on the packaging. The site partner does not need to run a separate kitchen for the hot meal option.

Agree how servicing will work

LECKERDING handles the agreed restocking, stock rotation, cleaning and technical servicing. Both parties agree when the service team can enter and whom to contact if a gate is closed. A named contact at the workplace helps the operator respond to building works, changes in break times or temporary access restrictions.

Hear from the late shift as well

An evening favourite selling out and a morning dish attracting little interest point to different needs. For planning the selection, it helps to know which item was missing and at what time. For a technical issue, the location and approximate time also help the service team identify the right machine and follow up.
